author: La Touche, 1907
summary: 2010년 11월 13일 제주 마라도에서 암컷 한 마리가 그물에 걸려 사진으로 기록된 것이 국내 첫 기록인 길잃은새로, 생김새와 몸 치수에 DNA 분석을 더해 종을 확인했다. 국외에서는 그늘진 늘푸른넓은잎나무 숲에 살며, 낮은 가지에 조용히 앉아 있다가 곤충을 잡는다. 중국 중부·남부와 베트남의 산지 숲에서 번식하고, 일부는 겨울에 중국 남부와 홍콩, 라오스, 베트남, 캄보디아로 옮겨 간다.

art.subject: Fujian Niltava (Niltava davidi), adult male, a vagrant in Korean island forest: forehead and crown shining cobalt-blue; face, chin and throat black; a small glossy blue patch on the side of the neck and another at the shoulder; mantle, back, wings and tail deep dark blue, the flight feathers blackish with blue edges; breast and upper belly deep orange-rufous, sharply divided from the black throat, paling to buff on the lower belly and undertail coverts. Bill black, short and broad; eye dark; legs dark.
art.pose: perched upright on a low branch in shaded undergrowth, side view
art.scene: dense evergreen forest understorey on a southern Korean island in late autumn (November), subdued light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, perched upright on a low branch, side view: bright blue crown and shoulder, blue-black face, chin, throat and mantle, thin bright blue line on the side of the neck, dark blue back and wings, blue tail, orange-rufous breast and flanks sharply demarcated from the dark throat, paler orange lower belly and vent

adult female, perched upright on a low branch, side view: brown head, upperparts and breast, rufous edges to the wing coverts and flight feathers, white gorget across the lower throat, sometimes a pale blue line on the side of the neck, whitish centre to the belly and vent
art.build: A stocky, large-headed flycatcher, larger than a sparrow, with a thick neck and a fairly long tail; sits upright and still in the lower or middle storey, dropping to the ground for prey. Bill black, short, broad-based and slightly hooked at the tip, much shorter than the head. Legs short and dark. Wings short and rounded, the wingtips reaching only a short way down the tail. Tail fairly long and square-ended, dark blue, without white.
avoid: Do not paint a white belly or white tail patches; the breast is deep orange-rufous, paling only to buff towards the vent, and the tail is plain dark blue.
Do not paint a blue throat or blue breast (Blue-and-white Flycatcher); the throat is black and the breast orange.
Do not make the bird bright sky-blue overall; only the crown, neck spot and shoulder are glossy, the rest is deep dark blue.
Do not give it a thin warbler bill or long legs.
